body.statement: If \(Z_1,\ldots,Z_m\) are independent random variables taking values in \([0,1]\), then, for every \(t>0\), \(\Pr\{|m^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^m Z_i-m^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^m\mathbb E Z_i|>t\}\leq2\exp(-2mt^2)\).

source.locator: Theorem 2, specialized to unit ranges and two tails
source.verbatim_statement: If X₁,…,Xₙ are independent and aᵢ ≤ Xᵢ ≤ bᵢ, then for t > 0, P(X̄ − μ ≥ t) ≤ exp(−2n²t² / ∑ᵢ(bᵢ−aᵢ)²).

attestation.note: Main read the scanned primary 1963 paper, page 16, Theorem 2 and equation (2.6). The cited node is its unit-range specialization, applied also to the negated variables and combined by a union bound for two tails.

body.justification: This is the finite-sample concentration input used by the explicit continuity-only interval.
body.gap: The theorem is classical substrate rather than a novelty claim.
body.consumer: The continuity-only frontier invokes it for the retained-course and atom-mass averages.
